notes: Weapon figures are the book's modifiers; null is the book's n/a. strength is the minimum Strength to use the weapon (a weapon's and a shield's are met separately); range is the range increment in paces. Every natural weapon uses Brawl; Strength, Load and Cost do not apply to them.

weapons.name: Dodge
weapons.description: Simply getting out of the way of opponents, without trying to do damage.

weapons.name: Fist
weapons.description: Any unarmed attack made with the hands.

weapons.name: Kick
weapons.description: Unarmed attacks made with the feet are more powerful, but less accurate. Characters may kick standing opponents, but most often this attack is used against prone enemies.

weapons.name: Gauntlet
weapons.description: A heavy glove of hardened leather or chain mail. It does more damage than a bare fist, and is more effective at blocking attacks. Full armor always includes gauntlets and partial armor sometimes does (troupe's option).

weapons.name: Bludgeon
weapons.description: A sap (a leather bag filled with lead shot) or any heavy object like a stone or a small hammer: any improvised bashing weapon such as a rock or hand tool.

weapons.name: Dagger
weapons.description: Any knife-like weapon between about 6 inches and 14 inches long. Daggers are commonly carried as tools, as well as for self-defense.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.description: Any sharp knife of 6 inches or less. Knives are even more common than daggers; they are everyday tools.

weapons.name: Axe
weapons.description: A common woodcutter's axe or a heavier battle weapon, small enough to wield in one hand, albeit sometimes awkwardly.

weapons.name: Club
weapons.description: Simply a heavy stick, or an iron-shod weapon.

weapons.name: Hatchet
weapons.description: Any axe with a haft shorter than about 18 inches. It does less damage than a longer axe because of poor leverage. Some hatchets are suitable for throwing.

weapons.name: Lance
weapons.description: Used only from horseback, where it is a Single weapon. A dismounted rider may wield it two-handed as a Long Spear.

weapons.name: Mace
weapons.description: Any heavy, bludgeoning weapon with a weighted head, usually made of iron and usually spiked or flanged. Includes spiked clubs, military hammers and other one-handed bashing weapons.

weapons.name: Mace and Chain
weapons.description: One or more weighted, spiked or flanged heads connected to a haft by a length of stout chain. Sometimes called a "morning star."

weapons.name: Short Spear
weapons.description: A spear short enough to wield in one hand, from 4 to 7 feet in length. A very common battlefield weapon, often used by warriors who cannot afford a sword.

weapons.name: Short Sword
weapons.description: Any bladed weapon from 14 inches to about 28 inches long, single- or double-edged, usually with a sharp point for thrusting. Large woodsman's knives are big enough to count as short swords.

weapons.name: Long Sword
weapons.description: Any sword over 28 inches long, typically used by horsemen because it is long enough to reach opponents on foot. Long swords are typically straight, even in Arabia.

weapons.name: Buckler
weapons.description: A small shield that buckles to the forearm, usually made of metal. It is light enough that other objects can be held in the shield hand.

weapons.name: Round Shield
weapons.description: A wooden shield that is cheap and easy to make.

weapons.name: Heater Shield
weapons.description: Often made of a combination of wood and metal, this shield tapers to a point at the bottom. Its outer surface is convex, to better deflect blows.

weapons.name: Cudgel
weapons.description: A heavy, two-handed club.

weapons.name: Farm Implement
weapons.description: Rakes, scythes, mattocks and other farm implements used as improvised weapons: awkward, and apt to break under the rigors of combat.

weapons.name: Flail
weapons.description: A two-handed, heavier version of the common threshing flail: effective and easy to make. Treat a smaller, one-handed flail as a Mace and Chain.

weapons.name: Pole Arm
weapons.description: Bladed, long-handled weapons, from the continental guisarme to the English "brown bill": they vary in detail but share a long cutting blade, and the same statistics.

weapons.name: Pole Axe
weapons.description: Any axe too large to wield one-handed, typically four to six feet long.

weapons.name: Long Spear
weapons.description: Any spear too long to use one-handed, from about 8 to 15 feet or longer. Includes the lance, if used dismounted.

weapons.name: Great Sword
weapons.description: A heavy, two-handed sword, designed to penetrate heavy armor.

weapons.name: Staff
weapons.description: A common, inexpensive weapon often carried about the countryside for self-defense.

weapons.name: Warhammer
weapons.description: Includes other weighted, two-handed bludgeoning weapons, such as a two-handed mace.

weapons.name: Short Dueling Stick
weapons.description: A short fighting stick of the ancient period, reprinted in Lords of Men's Melee Weapon Table (p. 137) from Ancient Magic (p. 95). Crushing.

weapons.name: Falchion
weapons.description: A heavy, one-handed blade like a machete, carried by common soldiers; late medieval (Lords of Men pp. 137, 139). Slashing.

weapons.name: Net
weapons.description: A poor weapon, but good for tripping, grappling or disarming a foe, or unseating a rider, rolled with Single Weapon + the net's Attack instead of Brawl (Lords of Men pp. 137, 139; Guardians of the Forests p. 134). Ancient.

weapons.name: Infantry Shield
weapons.description: A large oval or rectangular shield carried only on foot, such as the Roman legionary's convex scutum (Lords of Men pp. 137, 139). Ancient.

weapons.name: Trident
weapons.description: A three-pronged spear, reprinted in Lords of Men's Melee Weapon Table (p. 137) from Guardians of the Forests (p. 134). Ancient; piercing.

weapons.name: Whip
weapons.description: Not much of a weapon, but good for tripping, grappling or disarming a foe, or unseating a rider, rolled with Single Weapon + the whip's Attack instead of Brawl (Lords of Men pp. 137, 139).

weapons.name: Halberd
weapons.description: Like a pole axe with a steel spike on top and, usually, a hook that can drag a rider from his horse; late medieval (Lords of Men pp. 137, 139).

weapons.name: Bastard Sword (one-handed)
weapons.description: A large late-medieval sword wielded in one hand: a long sword's figures, but Strength +1 and Load 2 (Lords of Men p. 139, as corrected by the Errata p. 76). Wielded two-handed it is a great sword.

weapons.name: Bastard Sword (two-handed)
weapons.description: A large late-medieval sword wielded in both hands, as a great sword (Lords of Men p. 139).

weapons.name: Throwing Axe
weapons.description: Can be wielded in melee as a hatchet.

weapons.name: Javelin
weapons.description: Can be wielded in melee as a short spear.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.description: A knife thrown rather than wielded.

weapons.name: Sling
weapons.description: Although the sling uses the Thrown Weapon skill, it has much greater range than a hand-hurled weapon. Requires two free hands to load and fire; its Load includes its ammunition.

weapons.name: Stone
weapons.description: A stone heavy enough to hurt someone, about the size of a fist.

weapons.name: Long Bow
weapons.description: The famous English longbow, which equally famously required years of training and physical conditioning to use. Requires two free hands to load and fire; its Load includes its arrows.

weapons.name: Short Bow
weapons.description: Weaker than the long bow, but still powerful enough to use on the battlefield or to hunt large game. Requires two free hands to load and fire; its Load includes its arrows.

weapons.name: Greek Fire Siphon
weapons.description: A hand-held siphon squirting Greek Fire, worked by the Byzantine naffatun with Profession: Naffatun instead of a Martial Ability. Shields don't defend against it in the usual way, for the liquid fire splashes round them: a shield's Defence adds to its bearer's Soak instead. One dose of Greek Fire is good for 10 sprays (The Sundered Eagle p. 47).

weapons.name: Sharpened Rock
weapons.description: A very primitive weapon, sometimes used by faeries and the like (Lords of Men pp. 138-139, from Ancient Magic p. 17). Crushing or slashing.

weapons.name: Composite Bow
weapons.description: The bow of Saracens, Moors and the nomads of Asia: Turks and Mongols, or earlier Huns and Magyars (Lords of Men pp. 138-139; Ancient Magic p. 17). Requires two free hands to load and fire.

weapons.name: Horse Bow
weapons.description: A compact composite bow made for shooting from horseback (Lords of Men pp. 138-139; Ancient Magic p. 17). Requires two free hands to load and fire.

weapons.name: Crossbow
weapons.description: Spanned with a belt hook in three rounds (one by hand with Strength +3 or more; two with a late-medieval goat's foot). Strength doesn't add to its Damage, and an untrained user takes no extra botch dice (Lords of Men pp. 138-139, replacing Covenants p. 18).

weapons.name: Arbalest
weapons.description: A crossbow spanned with a windlass in four rounds, or with block and tackle in (6 - Strength) rounds; an interrupted spanning can be resumed. Strength doesn't add to its Damage (Lords of Men pp. 138-139).

weapons.name: Heavy Arbalest
weapons.description: A powerful late-medieval arbalest with a steel bow, spanned with its built-in cranequin in six rounds; an interrupted spanning can be resumed. Strength doesn't add to its Damage (Lords of Men pp. 138-139).

weapons.name: Grapple
weapons.description: A grapple attack instead of a normal attack, against an opponent no larger than the creature's Size + 1 (the Grapple Quality). Also the creature's Defense against anyone outside the grapple.

weapons.name: Dodge
weapons.description: Simply getting out of the way of opponents, without trying to do damage.

armor.name: Quilted/Fur
armor.description: Quilted cloth, a thin layer of leather, or layers of leather-strap-wrapped fur or cloth: the most basic of armor. Partial only.

armor.name: Heavy Leather
armor.description: Very thick leather, or leather hardened by wax impregnation or baking: better at deflecting crushing damage. Partial only.

armor.name: Metal Reinforced Leather
armor.description: Leather reinforced with studs, rings, or other metal pieces, which strengthen it against slashes and cuts.

armor.name: Leather Scale
armor.description: Leather broken up into a flexible array of scales, which allows thicker pieces of leather.

armor.name: Metal Scale
armor.description: Small overlapping metal plates in place of leather scales: more protection while keeping flexibility, although metal weighs slightly more.

armor.name: Chain Mail
armor.description: A suit of flexible metal made of links of chain: the top of 1220 technology.

armor_pieces.name: Padded Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Wool or linen quilted into dense layers, heavy felt, suede or leather stuffed with horsehair, or thick fur such as bearskin. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Padded Haubergeon
armor_pieces.description: Wool or linen quilted into dense layers, heavy felt, suede or leather stuffed with horsehair, or thick fur such as bearskin. Worn as a haubergeon (a short-sleeved armoured tunic covering torso and shoulders) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Padded Hauberk
armor_pieces.description: Wool or linen quilted into dense layers, heavy felt, suede or leather stuffed with horsehair, or thick fur such as bearskin. Worn as a hauberk (a knee-length, long-sleeved coat covering body, arms and upper legs) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Padded
armor_pieces.description: Wool or linen quilted into dense layers, heavy felt, suede or leather stuffed with horsehair, or thick fur such as bearskin. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Boiled Leather Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Very tough but stiff leather; also rawhide and like materials, even faerie armour of tree bark. Too rigid for sleeves. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Boiled Leather
armor_pieces.description: Very tough but stiff leather; also rawhide and like materials, even faerie armour of tree bark. Too rigid for sleeves. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Reinforced Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Leather or padding strengthened by many small hard plates or rings, usually metal, sometimes horn, bone or whalebone. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Reinforced Haubergeon
armor_pieces.description: Leather or padding strengthened by many small hard plates or rings, usually metal, sometimes horn, bone or whalebone. Worn as a haubergeon (a short-sleeved armoured tunic covering torso and shoulders) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Reinforced Hauberk
armor_pieces.description: Leather or padding strengthened by many small hard plates or rings, usually metal, sometimes horn, bone or whalebone. Worn as a hauberk (a knee-length, long-sleeved coat covering body, arms and upper legs) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Reinforced
armor_pieces.description: Leather or padding strengthened by many small hard plates or rings, usually metal, sometimes horn, bone or whalebone. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Rigid Scale Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Any scale or lamellar armour that isn't metal: boiled-leather scales are worn throughout Mythic Europe, horn and whalebone sometimes. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Rigid Scale Haubergeon
armor_pieces.description: Any scale or lamellar armour that isn't metal: boiled-leather scales are worn throughout Mythic Europe, horn and whalebone sometimes. Worn as a haubergeon (a short-sleeved armoured tunic covering torso and shoulders) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Rigid Scale Hauberk
armor_pieces.description: Any scale or lamellar armour that isn't metal: boiled-leather scales are worn throughout Mythic Europe, horn and whalebone sometimes. Worn as a hauberk (a knee-length, long-sleeved coat covering body, arms and upper legs) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Rigid Scale
armor_pieces.description: Any scale or lamellar armour that isn't metal: boiled-leather scales are worn throughout Mythic Europe, horn and whalebone sometimes. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Metal Scale Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Every kind of metal lamellar; brigandine is a late-medieval metal scale. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Metal Scale Haubergeon
armor_pieces.description: Every kind of metal lamellar; brigandine is a late-medieval metal scale. Worn as a haubergeon (a short-sleeved armoured tunic covering torso and shoulders) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Metal Scale Hauberk
armor_pieces.description: Every kind of metal lamellar; brigandine is a late-medieval metal scale. Worn as a hauberk (a knee-length, long-sleeved coat covering body, arms and upper legs) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Metal Scale
armor_pieces.description: Every kind of metal lamellar; brigandine is a late-medieval metal scale. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Mail Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Chain mail: shirts and hauberks date from the ancient period, full mail from the early Middle Ages. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Mail Haubergeon
armor_pieces.description: Chain mail: shirts and hauberks date from the ancient period, full mail from the early Middle Ages. Worn as a haubergeon (a short-sleeved armoured tunic covering torso and shoulders) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Mail Hauberk
armor_pieces.description: Chain mail: shirts and hauberks date from the ancient period, full mail from the early Middle Ages. Worn as a hauberk (a knee-length, long-sleeved coat covering body, arms and upper legs) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Mail
armor_pieces.description: Chain mail: shirts and hauberks date from the ancient period, full mail from the early Middle Ages. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Plate Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Solid pieces of metal. The full plate is late-medieval Gothic harness (c. 1400); an ancient plate cuirass is the cuirass. Too rigid for sleeves. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Plate
armor_pieces.description: Solid pieces of metal. The full plate is late-medieval Gothic harness (c. 1400); an ancient plate cuirass is the cuirass. Too rigid for sleeves. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Plate and Mail Cuirass or Jerkin
armor_pieces.description: Mail strengthened with metal plates; breastplates over mail are rare before about 1300. Worn as a cuirass (breast and back plates) or a short sleeveless jerkin (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Plate and Mail Haubergeon
armor_pieces.description: Mail strengthened with metal plates; breastplates over mail are rare before about 1300. Worn as a haubergeon (a short-sleeved armoured tunic covering torso and shoulders) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Plate and Mail Hauberk
armor_pieces.description: Mail strengthened with metal plates; breastplates over mail are rare before about 1300. Worn as a hauberk (a knee-length, long-sleeved coat covering body, arms and upper legs) (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Full Plate and Mail
armor_pieces.description: Mail strengthened with metal plates; breastplates over mail are rare before about 1300. Worn as full armour, cap-a-pie: all four limbs as well as torso and loins, greaves included (Lords of Men pp. 139-141).

armor_pieces.name: Gambeson
armor_pieces.description: A padded garment -- tunic, sleeveless surcoat or long-sleeved coat -- worn over, under or instead of other armour (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Coat of Plates
armor_pieces.description: A lamellar cuirass worn over mail, from about 1250 to 1300 (Lords of Men pp. 140-141). These are the Surcoats table's figures (+2, Load 2, p. 140); the Glossary (p. 141) says to use a metal scale cuirass's (+3, Load 3) instead. The book conflicts, and the app follows the table.

armor_pieces.name: Boiled-Leather Greaves
armor_pieces.description: Boiled-leather armour for the lower legs; already part of full body armour (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Plate Jambes
armor_pieces.description: Plate armour for the legs, from about 1320; already part of full body armour (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Plate-and-Mail Jambes
armor_pieces.description: Leg armour of mail strengthened with plates; already part of full body armour (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Iron Cap
armor_pieces.description: A helmet guarding mainly the crown of the head, leaving the face bare (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Coif or Camail
armor_pieces.description: A mail hood: a coif leaves the face open, a camail covers head, forehead and lower face (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Open Helmet
armor_pieces.description: A helmet guarding the sides and back of the head, the face at least half bare. Perception -1 (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Helm
armor_pieces.description: A high-medieval helm enclosing head and neck in iron plates. Perception -3 (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).

armor_pieces.name: Bascinet
armor_pieces.description: A late-medieval helmet shaped to head and neck, usually with a movable visor; late medieval only. Perception -1 (Lords of Men pp. 140-141).
